Templates can now be written by a program or a language model and checked the way a program
needs: what is wrong, and a JSON Pointer to where. Both browser faces can be embedded in a host
application, insert the host's merge fields and sub-documents, and keep the engine's own pages
on screen as the template changes.

Nothing was removed or renamed in the public API, and the template format has no new
properties: a template written by 0.2.0 reads in 0.1.0, and the other way round.

## Engine (`Frisket` package)

- **`TemplateJson.Check(json)`** reads a template's text before it is loaded. It names every
  property the engine does not read, which would otherwise be skipped in silence (`"Txt"`, or
  `"text"` in the wrong case), with the name probably meant, and reports a text the reader
  refuses with the place it gave.
- **`TemplateFields.Check(report, catalogueJson)`** holds every token and data path to the
  host's catalogue of fields. It resolves names the way the binder does: inside a repeated
  container, an entry's fields first, then the root.
- **`TemplateIssue.Pointer`** - every finding carries a JSON Pointer into the template - and
  **`TemplateIssue.ToJson(issues)`**, the one shape the command line, the server and a host
  all write.
- **New rule `sound.noPageSize`** (an error): a section without a page size was laid out on a
  sheet of nothing. A template that passed `TemplateValidator.Check` in 0.1.0 may now be
  refused for this, rightly.
- **`{Pages}` and `{SectionPages}` work in rich text.** In an `AdvancedTextItem` they printed
  the placeholder - "page 1 of 0". The rule that warned about it,
  `sound.advancedTextPageCount`, is gone with the fault.
- **The SVG proof draws a styled piece the way the PDF does.** The browser collapsed the space a
  piece starts with and kerned what the engine never kerns; each page now carries the rule
  that stops both.
- The JSON Schema describes every type and property, from the engine's own documentation.

## Command line and server

- `frisket check --json` writes the findings as JSON (UTF-8, whatever the console's code
  page), and `--fields catalogue.json` adds the catalogue check.
- The demonstration server answers `POST /check`, and now expands the sub-templates a template
  carries before drawing it: a carried piece was an empty box in the exact preview.

## Template designer and content editor (in the repository)

Not in the packages; `release/` holds each as a single HTML file.

- **The designer is a call and an element**, `frisketDesigner(seams)` and
  `<frisket-designer>`, ready for a host application's front end. Several can share a page.
- **Sub-documents from the host.** A host hands the designer its library
  (`{ list(), find(reference) }`); pieces are offered in the palette, named `st://reference`
  in the template, drawn in the preview and saved as names only.
- **The engine's pages, kept up to date** as the template changes - on the canvas, beside
  it, or in a window of its own, as the person chooses. The host names its engine (`server`)
  and may supply its own `fetch` for credentials; with no server, nothing is asked.
- **Merge fields in the content editor.** A host hands it a catalogue (`fields`); a field
  goes in at the caret as its token and Ctrl+Z takes it out again, a picture field becomes a
  picture the data fills, and a list becomes a table repeated over it.
- **Repeating tables** (`RepeatOver`) can be set in the designer's panel, for a group, a
  table or a grid.
- The content editor is told where its engine is, as the designer is.

Fixed in the faces: the designer stopped on a template whose rich text named no font of its
own; a body that did not state its layout put every item at an undefined position; a text in
a flow did not wrap; on a 1920 x 1080 screen every click zoomed the designer in until it
spilled over the host page; the editor's toolbar wrapped on a host page with a smaller root
font.

## Examples

`examples/ai/README.md` is a guide for wiring a model to these checks. Test 97 runs the whole
loop - write, check, correct at the pointers, check again - and leaves its material in
`tests/output/model/`.
